notes: Site is a Shopify store (thedecorkart.com); direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no Playwright/Claude-in-Chrome needed. Scanned all 639 collections in collections.json plus homepage nav/mega-menu/announcement bar for Clearance-family terms (Clearance, Outlet, Final Sale, Last Chance, End of Line, Discontinued) and found zero matches anywhere on the site -- there is no page anywhere on this site that uses clearance/outlet/permanent-markdown taxonomy language. The only discount-aggregation concept the site exposes is 'On Sale' (/collections/on-sale), a top-level nav item promoted alongside Bestsellers/New Arrivals/Trending Now (announcement bar, mega-menu promo card). Its own page has no meta description and a bare H1 'On Sale' with no permanence/outlet signal in any visible copy, breadcrumb, or heading -- so per the Sale-vs-Clearance test this cannot be confidently classified either way: it could be a genuine evergreen markdown hub (it is a permanent nav fixture, not tied to a named seasonal campaign) or simply a generic 'everything currently discounted' filter roll-up (the prior Home-Decor pass on this exact site explicitly excluded discount-percentage-band collections as marketing roll-ups, and this appears to be the same underlying mechanism). Recorded per brief instruction to record-and-flag rather than guess. The /collections/on-sale hub page itself declares 6 genuine per-category children via its own 'shop by category' collection-card slider (Decor/Kitchen & Dining/Lighting/Furniture/Wall Decor/Bath Decor Sale) -- kept as group+leaves, same ambiguity applies to all (none use clearance/outlet wording either). All qty values are exact counts from exhaustive /collections/<handle>/products.json pagination (limit=250) deduped by product id; collections.json's products_count field is confirmed inflated for every one of these collections (e.g. on-sale claims 2178 vs 1887 real) and was not used, consistent with this site's known pattern from the prior Home-Decor extraction pass.

rows.evidence: Exhaustive dedup via /collections/on-sale/products.json?limit=250 paged => 1887 unique product ids (collections.json products_count field = 2178, confirmed inflated, not used). Page H1 is plain 'On Sale' with no meta description.
rows.flag: MANUAL REVIEW: AMBIGUOUS SALE/CLEARANCE - page is titled plainly 'On Sale' with zero permanence/outlet/clearance language anywhere on the page or in its breadcrumb/heading; it is a permanent top-level nav fixture (not a named seasonal campaign), which leans toward a genuine markdown hub, but the complete absence of Clearance/Outlet/Final Sale/Last Chance wording anywhere on the entire site (639 collections scanned) means it cannot be confirmed as clearance-taxonomy per the brief's test. Recording rather than guessing.
